newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady to weaker, $190.50 Aug trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady to weaker, $190.50 Aug trade.

text.p: The European gasoline market on Monday began steady to slightly weaker than Friday, as early second half July Eurograde barge trades were followed around lunchtime by a confirmed first half August trade at $190.50 FOB AR.
A Benelux trader confirmed selling the August lot to a Scandinavian oil producer in the wake of second half July trades at $190.25, $192.50 and $193 earlier in the morning.

In the absence of reported regular barge trades, values were still quoted $12-$13 below premium unleaded, while a quiet cargo market was seen broadly unchanged from end-Friday quotes in the $195-$198 CIF NWE range.

Gasoline August swap values were meanwhile quoted in the $190-$191 range by 1200 GMT, having earlier been talked in the wider $190-$192 range. September was seen $4 backwardated to August and October another $4 behind September in a deal-dry start to trading.
Dealers said there had been little change to sentiments or prices in trading early Monday, and saw no clear direction yet emerging by lunchtime.
